content.title: About
content.content: Hard filled pretzels NFS (3026) are crunchy snack sticks shaped in the classic knot, filled with sweet or savory fillings. They are made from wheat flour, water, salt and yeast, then baked to a golden crust. Fillings may include chocolate, caramel, nuts, cheese or fruit jam.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Hard pretzels originate from Germany, where they are called "Brezel".
Filled versions appeared in the United States in the early 1920s as a convenient travel snack.
NFS (National Food Standards) assigned code 3026 to identify this product category in international databases.
The traditional knot shape symbolizes the crossed arms of monk‑bakers who prayed for safe journeys.
In some countries pretzels are served with mustard, but filled versions often feature sweet fillings.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: The hard texture provides a slow release of energy, helping to maintain satiety.

items.title: Contains plant protein
items.content: Wheat flour and certain fillings (e.g., nuts) add a modest amount of protein.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Yeast‑leavened dough is rich in thiamine and niacin, supporting metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Iron, magnesium and phosphorus are present, important for bones and blood formation.

items.title: Antioxidants in the filling
items.content: Chocolate or berry fillings contain polyphenols that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Hard pretzels contain wheat, making them unsuitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Sweet fillings can significantly increase calories and sugar levels.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Savory versions may contain up to 1 g of salt per 100 g, which should be considered by those with hypertension.

items.title: Choking hazard
items.content: The hard texture can be dangerous for young children; offer finely broken pieces.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pretzels are convenient as a standalone snack, added to salads, used in dessert recipes, or served with yogurt. For a softer texture, lightly warm them in the oven.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For longer shelf life, keep refrigerated to preserve crunchiness and prevent the filling from going rancid.
